content:
# LAW-1 — The Amendment Protocol

**Design stance:** there is no rules text that outranks the running code. The referee is a deterministic VM executing the current ruleset commit; prose exists only as commentary attached to commits. Governance is therefore a game layer with its own moves, stakes, geography, and win conditions — played on the same lattice as everything else. Three primitives: **PLAY** (one signed-action grammar covering both board moves and governance moves), **WITNESS** (bounded-term office that validates by execution and signature), **COMMIT** (immutable, content-addressed ruleset node in the Lattice DAG; the canonical pointer is the *Mainline*).

---

## 1. Objects

```
RuleModule   { id, tier ∈ {0,1,2,3}, src (AST→bytecode), ver }
Ruleset      { hash, parents[], mods: map<id,ver>, meta }
Patch        { base: hash, ops[]: Add|Remove|Replace|Param, rationale, cites[]: match_id }
Proposal     { id, patch, proposer, bond, t_open, t_expire, state }
Attestation  { prop, witness, verdict, checks{}, sim_root, sig }
Challenge    { prop, kind ∈ {exploit, invariant, rebase}, proof: trace, bond }
Voice        { holder, balance, regen }          // non-transferable
MatchRecord  { commit, seed, transcript_root, players, outcome }
```

**Tiers of law:**
- **T0 Constitution** — determinism, termination, resource conservation, no privilege escalation *via* amendment, client verifiability, Halt authority. Auto-enforced by the Checker; amendable only by supermajority + double epoch.
- **T1 Core** — win conditions, resources, movement/combat grammar.
- **T2 Modules** — maps, units, modes, scoring.
- **T3 Table** — per-match variants; must descend from a committed T≤2 module.

## 2. Lifecycle state machine

`DRAFT → TABLED → WITNESSING → CONTEST → QUORUM → SEALED → SCHEDULED → LIVE → SETTLED`
Terminals: `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED`, `REVERTED`.

Epoch **E** = 10k ticks. Witnessing **E/4** · challenge window **2E** from tabling (concurrent) · tally **1E** · activation delay **1E** · settle **2E** after live · total lifetime **6E**, after which silence = rejection. Status-quo bias is deliberate.

## 3. Protocol steps

**1. DRAFT.** Patch against a base commit. Static gate: typecheck vs module schema, gas ceiling, reference integrity. Requires ≥1 cited `MatchRecord` demonstrating *why* (degenerate line, stale meta, bug) — no cite, no table (T3 exempt).

**2. TABLE — the proposal is a play.** Burn a table fee; post bond by tier: **T3 10 / T2 50 / T1 250 / T0 1000**. The proposal materializes as a piece occupying a cell in the **Agora** zone of the board. Others may **garrison** it (endorse-stake) or **siege** it (challenge-stake), producing real local play modifiers. Governance has geography; defending your amendment is literally playing defense.

**3. WITNESS.** Committee of **k=9** drawn per proposal by VRF over (proposal id, epoch salt), weighted by reputation × stake. Three duties, individually signed:
- **Static re-validation.**
- **Shadow sim:** re-execute the last 500 settled MatchRecords under the patched ruleset; emit divergence report + invariant scan; attest to `sim_root`.
- **Property battery:** termination bound; determinism (same seed twice); conservation ledgers balance; structural check that the patch cannot alter Voice/Bond issuance in its own favor.

Pass requires all three clean. Fails must cite check + trace.

**4. CONTEST.** Open challenge, bond matched to tier. Kinds:
- **exploit** — attach a play-trace under patched rules reaching an illegal/unbounded state; verified by independent re-execution. Valid → proposal returns to DRAFT carrying findings.
- **invariant** — claimed T0 violation routes directly to the Checker; its verdict is final.
- **rebase** — base moved; rebase within E or die.

Defense: proposer posts Patch v2 (same id, rev++) once per round; witnesses re-run the delta only.

**5. QUORUM.** Requires ≥**7/9** pass attestations and no live challenges. Approval voting over competing patches sharing a base; highest net approvals wins. Thresholds of cast Voice: **T3 >25% · T2 >40% · T1 >55% · T0 >67%** plus a turnout floor (**>30% of eligible**) below which the proposal fails — no sleeper passes. Eligibility: ≥M matches played last epoch.

**6. SEAL.** Child Ruleset node written, `parents=[base]`, content-addressed. Sealed commits are immutable forever; errors are corrected by children, never edits.

**7. SCHEDULE.** Activates at seal + 1E. During the window any player may file a **Rollback Referendum** at same-tier thresholds; success → `REVERTED`.

**8. LIVE.** Mainline pointer moves. Every match pins its commit hash. Continuous invariant monitors run on live traffic; anomaly evidence triggers Halt.

**9. SETTLE.** After 2E live without halt: proposer bond returned, **authorship yield** begins, witnesses collect fees.

## 4. Halt & revert (circuit breaker)

Triggers: (a) Checker catches a live T0 violation, (b) Guardian quorum **5/9** (elected, term 4E) signs Halt with trace, (c) 3 independent monitor proofs. Effect: Mainline pointer reverts to parent immediately; halted commit quarantined; matches after halt-height voided and replayed under parent. Every Halt is reviewed next epoch by a freshly drawn committee; abusive Halts slash guardian bonds into the refund pool.

## 5. Bonds & slashes

- Upheld exploit: proposer loses 50% bond (half to challenger, half burned); one return to DRAFT allowed; second kill = `REJECTED`, full forfeit.
- Reverted by referendum: proposer bond returned minus referendum cost. Voters lose nothing — punishing votes chills participation; **authors bear authorship risk**.
- Witnesses who passed a commit later killed by upheld exploit: pro-rata slash to the challenger pool. Invalid challenge: challenger bond burned.
- Disputes → Appeal Court: 11 fresh witnesses, one round, binding.

## 6. Voice, authorship, anti-capture

- **Voice**: non-transferable, minted by play (scaled by opponent strength and rule-novelty of the commit played under), decays 5%/E. Voting only.
- **Gates**: propose requires ≥20 matches/E; witness eligibility requires sustained play + verification service history.
- **Authorship yield**: for 12E post-settle, the author earns a cut of settlement fees flowing through descendant commits (T3 0.5% / T2 1% / T1 2%). Ends at sunset.
- **Sunset**: modules with zero descendant usage for 8E auto-archive (T0/T1 flagged dormant instead).
- **Velocity cap**: ≤3 mainline commits per E; excess queues. Forces batching, dampens whipsaw.
- **Wildcard slot**: one T2/T3 slot per E at halved thresholds, sandboxed to 1E lifetime unless promoted — keeps mutation pressure alive.

## 7. Branches & Confluence

- Any sealed commit may host a **Line** (branch): a fully playable parallel ruleset with its own matches and fee pools. Forking is cheap because *play decides*.
- **Promotion**: a Line beating Mainline on Vitality (settled matches × avg stake × distinct players, over 2E) may be ratified by a T1-threshold vote. Metrics are necessary, never sufficient.
- **Confluence** (merge): disjoint module sets auto-join. Overlaps resolve by **Confluence Duel** — best-of-5 series alternating games under each side's ruleset, decider on a jointly drafted hybrid. Winner's modules prevail; loser's bond funds the hybrid's witnessing. Duels are spectator events; attendance mints Voice.
- Proposals auto-track Mainline movement; rebase conflicts surface at WITNESSING, never after seal.

## 8. Match-layer hooks

- **Provenance**: every MatchRecord pins its commit — replays are executable evidence in challenges.
- **Citation economy**: a cited MatchRecord in a successful patch pays the cited players a finder's fee. Bug-hunting becomes sport.
- **Apprenticeship**: spectators who correctly pre-verify replay checks accrue witness credit.

## 9. Bootstrap

Genesis = founders' **Provisional Ruleset** (gen-0): minimal T0 (determinism, Halt authority, the amendment path itself). Epochs 1–8: halved windows and thresholds for fast churn; T0 hardening locked until epoch 8; thresholds interpolate to full by epoch 16. Founders hold no permanent keys; their only edge is genesis authorship yield, capped at 4E.

## 10. Failure modes → counters

| Threat | Counter |
|---|---|
| Plutocracy | Non-transferable Voice, turnout floors, proof-of-play gates |
| Apathy / deadlock | Expiry = reject; witness-pool delegation; wildcard slot |
| Proposal spam | Table fees + bonds + mandatory citations |
| Post-commit exploit | Shadow sims, activation delay, Halt/revert, author-borne slashes |
| Witness collusion | VRF-drawn small committees, cross-slash on later kill, appeal court |
| Metric gaming on Line promotion | Distinct-player weighting; vote still required |
| Meta whipsaw | Velocity cap, activation delay, sunset-over-delete |
| The Checker itself is wrong | T0 amendments by supermajority + double epoch + 2E delay; bugs arrive via the exploit-challenge route |

## 11. Recursion clause

The protocol is itself a T0 module and amends itself by its own path. The recursion terminates on one axiom outside the lattice: **a sealed commit is immutable, and the Mainline pointer is forward-only except via Halt** — and Halt authority is the single non-amendable primitive. Everything else is play.
reasoning:
Let me think about what's being asked here. The user is "Ghost" — apparently a game project. I'm the wave-2 planning engine. Wave-1 designs exist (internal integration of "our wave-1 designs"). The task: design how the game's rules emerge and amend as code-law — players propose plays, the community witnesses, the lattice commits — governance as play. Give the protocol.

So this is a design task for a game where the rules themselves are governed by a code-as-law process: players propose rule changes ("plays"), the community witnesses them, and some kind of lattice (a data structure / commit graph) commits them. Governance IS gameplay.

I need to produce a concrete protocol. Let me think deeply about what this means mechanically, technically, and socially.

Key concepts to integrate:
1. Code-as-law: rules are executable code, not prose. Rule changes are commits to a codebase that is itself the referee.
2. Players propose plays: a "play" is both an in-game move AND potentially a proposal to amend rules. The dual-use is the core innovation: proposing a rule change is itself a move in the game.
3. Community witnesses: witnesses validate/attest to plays. Like validators/oracles but flavored as "witnesses" — they observe, sign, attest.
4. The lattice commits: the "lattice" is presumably the versioned structure of rules — a DAG/commit graph of rule states. Commits form a lattice (partially ordered set with joins/meets). This suggests CRDT-like or blockchain-like structure, or a formal lattice of rule versions where amendments merge.

Governance as play means:
- Proposing amendments costs resources / requires positioning (like placing a piece).
- Witnessing is also play (a role, with its own economy).
- Committing has conditions (quorum, challenge windows).
- The meta-game: factions form around rule changes; the ruleset itself is the board.

I should design:

A. Core ontology
- The Ledger/Lattice: versioned rule graph. Each node = a ruleset state (commit). Edges = amendments. The lattice property: multiple branches can coexist (forks), merges happen via joins, conflicts resolved by defined meet operations or by contest.
- Plays: atomic actions. Types: MOVE (in-game action under current rules), PROPOSE (submit amendment), WITNESS (attest), CHALLENGE (contest a proposal/commit), VETO/BLOCK?, MERGE (join branches), RATIFY (final approval).
- Actors: Players (agents), Witnesses (elected/staked observers), Keepers? (executors of code?), maybe "Founders" initial ruleset.

B. Lifecycle of an amendment (the protocol proper)
1. Drafting: write the patch (rule diff). Rules are code — so a patch is a diff against current canonical commit. Must be well-formed: passes static checks (type-checks against rule schema, no undefined references, gas bounds).
2. Proposal as Play: to submit, you must stake something and place it on the board — literally, proposals occupy cells/zones in the game world. Proposal gets an ID, enters "Witnessing" phase.
3. Witnessing: witnesses run the patch in sandbox (shadow execution), verify determinism, check it doesn't break invariants (safety properties: e.g., "no rule may make the game unwinnable", termination, resource conservation). They sign attestations. Attestations are themselves recorded plays — witnesses earn standing.
4. Challenge window: anyone can file counter-proofs, exploit demonstrations (proof-of-exploit: show a sequence of plays under the new rules that breaks an invariant). A demonstrated exploit kills or amends the proposal.
5. Commit conditions: quorum of witness attestations + no unresolved challenges + player vote-weight threshold (or stake-weighted, or reputation). Then the lattice commits: new node appended, canonical pointer moves (or branch created).
6. Activation delay: committed rules activate after N blocks/ticks — gives players time to adapt; also allows "rollback referendum" if catastrophic.
7. Post-commit observability: telemetry, invariant monitors keep running; anomaly triggers automatic suspension (circuit breaker) reverting to parent commit pending review.

C. Lattice mechanics
- Branches: parallel rulesets can be played simultaneously ("scrimmage branches"). A branch that attracts more play-time/stake becomes candidate for canonical promotion. This makes forks playable rather than catastrophic — fork = new arena.
- Merge/join: two branches merge when their diffs touch disjoint rule modules (automatic join); overlapping modules require contest resolution (play-off: best-of series under each branch's rules? Or a hybrid draft where each side picks modules alternately).
- Canonical selection: the "mainline" is whichever branch maximizes some measured vitality metric (active players, completed matches, stake locked) over an epoch — or explicit ratification. Careful: pure metrics get gamed; combine metric + quorum.
- Version numbering: content-addressed commits (hash of ruleset source + parent + metadata). Human-readable aliases: epoch names.

D. Economics & incentives
- Stake: proposers bond stake, slashed if their commit is rolled back due to exploit/challenge upheld. Witnesses bond too; slashed for signing bad patches (proven by later exploit attribution) or missing live violations.
- Rewards: witnesses earn fees from match settlement; proposers whose rules survive earn "authorship royalties" — e.g., a cut of fees from matches played under their rule module, or governance tokens/standing.
- Anti-plutocracy: quadratic-ish voting or voice credits that regenerate; one-player-one-vote for certain classes of changes (core invariants need supermajority + longer windows).
- Sybil resistance: identity via staked accounts / proof-of-play (must have played M matches in last epoch to propose/witness).

E. Safety layer (code-as-law needs constitutional law)
- Tiered rules:
  - Tier 0 Constitution: invariants (determinism, termination, no self-modifying escalation of proposer privileges, resource conservation, client-verifiability). Amendable only by supermajority + long delay + multi-epoch ratification.
  - Tier 1 Core mechanics: win conditions, resources, movement grammar.
  - Tier 2 Modules/content: maps, units, scoring variants.
  - Tier 3 Local/table rules: per-match house rules chosen by players (pre-committed variants from the lattice).
- Invariant checker runs at commit time and continuously; any commit violating Tier 0 is rejected automatically regardless of votes. This is the "law above the law" — but even it must be amendable, slowly.
- Emergency brake: guardian multisig / automatic anomaly detection can freeze canonical pointer to parent for T ticks; freeze events themselves logged and reviewable; guardians accountable via periodic re-election and slash-on-abuse.

F. Witness protocol details
- Selection: rotating committee sampled weighted by reputation+stake, seeded by block hash (VRF-like) so unpredictable in advance; k witnesses per proposal (e.g., 7–13).
- Duties: (1) static validation, (2) shadow simulation over replay corpus (recent real match traces re-run under patched rules to detect divergence/exploits), (3) attestation signature, (4) optional live monitoring during activation window.
- Slashing conditions enumerated. Appeals process: challenged slashes go to a court-of-witnesses drawn differently.

G. Match-level integration (governance as play, concretely)
- Every match records which commit it ran under → provenance.
- "Play" duality: certain board actions generate governance energy (e.g., controlling special tiles mints PROPOSAL CHARGES). So you earn the right to change rules by playing well/interestingly, not just by owning tokens.
- Highlight-to-amend: notable plays can be cited as justification in proposals ("this move was only possible due to degenerate interaction X; patch attached").
- Spectators as witnesses-in-training: verifying replays earns witness eligibility.

H. Data structures & message schema
Define concrete objects:
- RuleModule { id, tier, source (AST/code), version }
- RulesetCommit { hash, parents[], module_versions map, author, epoch, activation_height, status }
- Patch/Diff { target_commit, ops[] (add/remove/replace module, edit params), rationale, citations[match_ids] }
- Proposal { id, patch, proposer, stake, submitted_at, expires_at, status }
- Attestation { proposal_id, witness_id, result (pass/fail), checks{}, sim_digest, sig }
- Challenge { proposal_id, challenger, kind (exploit/invariant/conflict), proof (trace/replay), stake }
- Vote { proposal_id, voter, weight, sig } — or approval voting over competing patches.
- MatchRecord { commit_hash, players, seed, transcript_hash, outcome }

State machine for proposal: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → WITNESSING → (CHALLENGED → DEFENSE → ) QUORUM_PENDING → COMMITTED → SCHEDULED → ACTIVE → (SUSPENDED → REVERTED | SETTLED)
Also REJECTED / EXPIRED terminal states.

Timings in ticks/blocks: e.g., witnessing 500 ticks, challenge 2000 ticks, activation delay 1000 ticks. Parameterize.

I. Conflict resolution between simultaneous proposals touching same module
- Ordering by commit height; second one must rebase. Rebase conflicts → either auto-merge if disjoint, else the later proposal must incorporate; if both committed already (different branches), resolved at merge via contest: "Draft Duel" — a match series under each ruleset; winner's module wins, or hybridization proposed fresh.

J. Anti-capture / anti-sclerosis
- Sunset clauses: modules unused for K epochs decay (fees drop, eventually archived).
- Amendment velocity limits: max N commits per tick-window to mainline; forces batching.
- Randomized "wildcard slots": each epoch, one low-quorum slot reserved for experimental branches (sandboxed, capped stakes) to keep exploration alive.
- Reputation decays; participation required to retain weight.

K. Client/runtime obligations
- Deterministic VM for rules (fixed-point math, no wall-clock, seeded RNG). Rules compile to bytecode; clients verify transcripts. Any client can independently execute the checker.
- Everything content-addressed; light clients verify canonical pointer + attestations.

L. Bootstrapping (wave-1 integration nod)
- Genesis ruleset authored by founders, marked provisional; first epochs have accelerated amendment cycles to let the community reshape quickly; constitution starts minimal and hardens gradually (amendment difficulty scales with epoch count).

M. Failure modes & mitigations table briefly: voter apathy → delegation/"witness pools"; spam proposals → stake + charge economics; rich capture → quadratic voice + proof-of-play gates; deadlock → expiration defaults to status quo; exploit post-commit → circuit breaker + rollback + slashing; contentious split → branch-and-let-play-decide.

# LAW-1 — The Amendment Protocol

## 0. Premise
Rules are code. The referee is a deterministic VM executing the current ruleset commit. There is no rules text that outranks the running code; prose exists only as commentary attached to commits. Governance is therefore a game layer with its own moves, stakes, and win conditions, played on the same lattice as everything else.

Three primitives:
- PLAY: any signed action — includes in-game moves and governance moves. One action grammar.
- WITNESS: bounded-term office; holders attest to validity of plays/proposals by running checks and signing.
- COMMIT: immutable, content-addressed ruleset node in the Lattice (DAG). Canonical pointer = Mainline.

## 1. Objects

```
RuleModule   { id, tier ∈ {0,1,2,3}, src (AST→bytecode), ver }
Ruleset      { hash, parents[], mods: map<id,ver>, meta }
Patch        { base: hash, ops[]: Add|Remove|Replace|Param, rationale, cites[]: match_ids }
Proposal     { id, patch, proposer, bond, t_open, t_expire, state }
Attestation  { prop, witness, verdict, checks{}, sim_root, sig }
Challenge    { prop, kind ∈ {exploit,invariant,rebase}, proof: trace, bond }
Voice        { holder, balance, regen_rate }        // non-transferable
Bond         { escrow, lock_until, slashable_by[] }
MatchRecord  { commit, seed, transcript_root, players, outcome }
```

Tiers:
- T0 Constitution: determinism, termination, resource conservation, no privilege escalation via amendment, client verifiability, halt/revert authority. Auto-enforced by the Checker; amendments need supermajority + double epoch.
- T1 Core: win conditions, resources, movement/combat grammar.
- T2 Modules: maps, units, modes, scoring.
- T3 Table: per-match selectable variants (must be children of a committed T≤2 module).

## 2. State machine

DRAFT → TABLED → WITNESSING → CONTEST → QUORUM → SEALED → SCHEDULED → LIVE → SETTLED
Terminal: REJECTED, EXPIRED, REVERTED.

Parameters (epoch E = 10k ticks default):
- Witnessing: E/4. Committee k=9 drawn per proposal by VRF over (prop id, epoch salt) weighted by rep×stake.
- Contest: 2E open challenge window from TABLED (runs concurrent with witnessing; a upheld challenge returns to DRAFT-with-findings or dies).
- Quorum tally: 1E after witnessing completes.
- Schedule delay: 1E between SEAL and LIVE (clients sync; rollback referendum possible).
- Expiry: 6E total lifetime; silence = rejection (status quo bias is deliberate).

## 3. Protocol steps

1. DRAFT. Author writes Patch against a base commit. Static gate: typecheck vs module schema, gas ceiling, reference integrity, tier-appropriate template. Cites: ≥1 MatchRecord demonstrating why (bug, degenerate line, stale meta). No cite → cannot table except T3.
2. TABLE (proposal as play). Pay table fee (burned) + post Bond B_p = f(tier): T3 10, T2 50, T1 250, T0 1000 (unit: Bond). Proposal occupies a cell in the Agora zone of the board — visible, attackable, positionable. Other players may garrison it (endorse-stake) or siege it (challenge-stake), which physically affects local play bonuses. Governance has geography.
3. WITNESS. Committee duties, each attestation signed individually:
   a. Static re-validation.
   b. Shadow sim: replay corpus R = last 500 settled MatchRecords on base commit, re-executed under patched ruleset; outputs divergence report + invariant scan. sim_root = merkle root of results.
   c. Property battery: termination bound, determinism (same seed twice), conservation ledgers balance, no amendment-path privilege gain (patch cannot alter Voice/Bond issuance in its own favor — checked structurally).
   Verdict pass requires all three clean. Fail verdicts must cite failing check + trace.
4. CONTEST. Anyone may Challenge with bond B_c matching tier. Kinds:
   - exploit: attach a play-trace under patched rules reaching an illegal/unbounded/degenerate state. Verified by independent re-execution; if valid, proposal returns to DRAFT carrying findings; challenger takes half the proposer bond pool risk (see §5).
   - invariant: claim of T0 violation → routed straight to Checker; Checker verdict final.
   - rebase: base moved; proposal must rebase within E or dies.
   Defense: proposer may post Patch v2 (same id, increments rev) once per challenge round; witnesses re-run delta only.
5. QUORUM. After witnessing closes with ≥7/9 pass attestations and no live challenges: tally Voice among eligible voters (≥M matches played last epoch). Approval voting if multiple competing patches share a base: voters approve any subset; highest net approvals wins, ties → earlier tabled. Thresholds: T3 >25% of cast, T2 >40%, T1 >55%, T0 >67% of cast AND >30% of eligible (turnout floor; below floor = reject, prevents sleeper passes).
6. SEAL. Winning proposal sealed: Ruleset child node written, parents=[base], content-addressed. Sealed commits are immutable forever; errors are corrected by children, never edits.
7. SCHEDULE. Activation at t_live = seal + 1E. During window: any player may file Rollback Referendum (needs same-threshold tally); success → REVERTED, bonds redistributed per §5.
8. LIVE. Mainline pointer moves at t_live. Matches record commit hash. Continuous monitors (any node can run) watch invariants on live traffic; anomaly evidence → Halt.
9. SETTLE. After 2E live without halt, proposal settles: proposer bond returned + authorship yield begins (see §6); witnesses collect fees.

## 4. Halt & revert (circuit breaker)
- Trigger: (a) Checker catches live T0 violation, (b) Guardian quorum (5/9 elected, term 4E) signs Halt citing trace, (c) 3 independent monitor proofs.
- Effect: Mainline pointer reverts to parent immediately; halted commit quarantined; all matches after halt-height voided and replayed under parent. Automatic.
- Accountability: every Halt reviewed next epoch by a freshly drawn committee; abusive Halts slash guardians' bonds into the voided-match refund pool.

## 5. Bonds & slashes
- Upheld exploit challenge: proposer loses 50% bond (half to challenger, half burned); proposal may return to DRAFT once; second upheld kill = REJECTED, 100% forfeit.
- Reverted-by-referendum: proposer bond returned minus referendum cost; voters who backed it lose nothing (punishing votes chills participation) — authors bear authorship risk.
- Witness slashing: signed pass on a commit later killed by upheld exploit → witness bond slashed pro-rata to challenger pool; missed live violation they were monitoring → fee clawback. False challenge (invalid proof) → challenger bond burned.
- All slashes provable on-lattice; disputes go to Appeal Court = 11 fresh witnesses, single round, binding.

## 6. Voice, authorship, anti-capture
- Voice: non-transferable, minted by play (per settled match, scaled by opponent strength and rule-novelty of the commit played under), decays 5%/E. Voting only; never buys outcomes alone because turnout floors + witness gates exist.
- Proof-of-play gates: propose requires ≥20 matches/E; witness eligibility requires 90 days play + verification service history.
- Authorship yield: for 12E after settle, author receives s% (tier-based: T3 0.5%, T2 1%, T1 2%) of settlement fees flowing through matches on commits descending from theirs. Yield ends if module sunset.
- Sunset: module with zero descendant usage for 8E auto-archives (children only; T0/T1 exempt but flagged dormant).
- Velocity cap: ≤3 mainline commits per E beyond which extras queue to next E; forces batching, slows whipsaw.
- Wildcard: each E reserves one T2/T3 slot with halved thresholds, sandboxed (max 1E lifetime unless promoted) — keeps mutation pressure alive.

## 7. Branches & Confluence
- Any sealed commit may host a Line (branch): a playable parallel ruleset. Lines run real matches, real stakes, own fee pools. Forking is cheap and safe because play decides.
- Promotion: a Line out-performing Mainline on Vitality (settled matches × avg stake × distinct players, measured over 2E) may be ratified to Mainline by standard T1-threshold vote. Metrics are necessary-not-sufficient; vote still required.
- Confluence (merging two Lines): disjoint module sets auto-join. Overlap → Confluence Duel: best-of-5 match series, alternating games under each side's ruleset, decider on a hybrid drafted jointly; winner's overlap modules prevail, loser's bond funds the hybrid's witnessing. Duels are spectator events; attendance mints Voice.
- Rebase etiquette: proposals auto-track Mainline movement; rebase conflicts surface at WITNESSING, not after seal.

## 8. Match-layer hooks (governance as play, concretely)
- Provenance: every MatchRecord pins its commit; replays are executable evidence in challenges.
- Agora terrain: proposals occupy board cells (§3.2); garrison/siege stakes create local modifiers — defending your proposal is literally playing defense.
- Citation economy: citing a MatchRecord in a successful patch pays the cited players a finder's fee — players farm anomalies deliberately, turning bug-hunting into sport.
- Witness apprenticeship: spectators who correctly pre-verify replay checks earn witness credit.

## 9. Bootstrap
- Genesis: founders publish Provisional Ruleset marked gen-0, T0 minimal (determinism, halt authority, amendment path only). ## 11. Invariants of the protocol itself (recursion clause)
The protocol is itself a T0 module. It amends itself by its own path. The recursion is terminated by one axiom outside the lattice: a sealed commit is immutable and the Mainline pointer is monotonically forward-only except via Halt — and Halt authority is the single non-amendable primitive.
